plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $49, the expected value of the highest of the other two bids is approximately (2/3) * 49 = $32.67. However, since there is only one round, a more conservative approach is to bid a small increment above half of your value to avoid overpaying. I will bid $8.50.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your value multiplied by 2/3. This is because if everyone follows this strategy, the expected winning bid will be 2/3 of the average value. To maximize profit, we should bid slightly below our value, accounting for the second-highest bid being the price we pay. With a value of $36, 2/3 * $36 = $24. I will bid $24.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any deviation downwards risks losing the auction to a slightly lower bid, while bidding higher risks overpaying. With a value of $42, bidding $42 ensures winning against bids below $42 and losing only to bids above $42, maximizing expected profit.
